To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Verapamil increased daunorubicine accumulation in leukemic cell lines with and without detectible mdr1 RNA.

Verapamil can increase accumulation of the anthracycline daunorubicn in human leukemic cell lines and primary leukemic cells, and that this increase is independent of the expression level of the multidrug resistance gene mdr1.
the distribution of the multidrug resistance phenotype in leukemia is heterogeneous and that the multidrug resistance gene is expressed in a subpopulation of leukemic cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of the MDR1 gene on daunorubcin accumulation in leukemic blasts and the effect of verapamil.
a study of the distribution of the multidrug resistance (MDR) phenotype in leukemic patients with different levels of the MDR1 gene (mdr1) expression.
the development of a novel method to detect the distribution of the mdr1 gene and the mdr1 protein in leukemic cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the MDR phenotype in leukemic cell lines is not necessarily a result of mdr1 over-expression.
the presence of the mdr1 gene is not sufficient for the expression of the multidrug resistance phenotype.
the mdr1 gene is not the only factor determining the resistance phenotype in leukemias.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the effect of verapamil is not only limited to the subpopulation with high mdr1 gene levels.
verapamil can reverse daunorubicine resistance in cells with different levels and patterns of mdr1 RNA expression.
the MDR phenotype in leukemia is not restricted to a single subpopulation of cells and the MDR1 gene may play a role in the resistance to daunorubicine also in leukemias without mdr1 RNA expression.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is no clear correlation between mdr1 gene transcription levels and the effect of verapamil in daunorubicn accumulation.
the MDR1 protein is not the only mechanism of MDR and that other mechanisms are involved in MDR.
the presence of a single gene is not enough to confer resistance to a drug, but that the gene has to be expressed at the right level and the right time.
